# <a id="_Toc140233949"></a>Release Management

##### Purpose of this document is to describe the procedure of releasing Teamcenter X kits to CApS for deployment in customer environment\. 

##### Policy Tag

##### Siemens Industry Software \(SISW\) SaaS Secure Development Policy\.pdf

##### Scope

This document defines the procedure for management of TcX Releases\. Sources of development requirements is not in scope for this document but in change management\. Similarly, once the code is handed over to CApS Team for release\. CApS team conduct its own dry runs and that is out of scope for this document\. The procedure for release management have following:

- Develop Branch containing pre\-release code
- Master Branch containing production code
- Hotfixes for master branch
- Release Criteria 

## <a id="_Toc140233950"></a>__Release Procedure__

### The workflow from development to production

##### Every tenth week the latest changes are promoted to pre\-production\. The teams coordinate their pushes to production through a meeting\. 

The figure below shows workflow from development to production of TcX\. It is essential to understand the Release requirements\. TcX team is responsible for product development and internal product validation, whereas the deployment and operation are managed by CApS team\. To ensure smooth handoff of developed code, close coordination of two teams is necessary\. CApS team is responsible to conduct a dry\-run and deploy the code for production\.

### Flow of work for release management

1. Development starts on a local machine, by creating a branch of a local repo for development of a specific bug fix or feature\. The branch should be created from the \(latest\) master branch\.
2. Code changes from the local machine are committed to the remote repository\. This initiates a CI pipeline specific to the branch, which includes the execution of static analysis, unit tests and a code build\. Optionally, a deployment to AWS development environment for further validation, and eventually a pass/fail result\. The CI build of this branch must be passing before the branch may be successfully merged as part of a Merge Request\.
3. Once the code is ready for review \(even preliminary review, as indicated by a "WIP:" prefix\), the author can create a merge request\.
4. Code review is scheduled __every day 2:30 PM IST__\. The code review panel comprises of all the developers and MR owner presents the changes and the test results\.
5. Manual acceptance of the Merge Request leads to code changes landing in our master branch\. Here, the CI Build process is repeated to account for any unintended drift or changes, and the resulting build artifacts are published to Product Validation for testing\.
6. The TcX code release team is responsible for promoting a kit to Product Validation, which is performed manually\. This decision is guided by the quality of the build \- code changes as per guidelines, unit tests pass, and static code analysis should contain 0 critical vulnerabilities and code review comments are addressed\.
7. The TcX code release team is additionally responsible for promoting kits changes to pre\-production \(aka\. Dry Run\)\. This decision is guided by the Product Validation feedback and readiness of the content decided by TcX Product Management\.
8. Based on testing status of Dry Run, build artifacts are signed off and kits will be moved to production\.

### Cadence for release cycles

The release cadence for Teamcenter X is as below:

1. Features reliant on the base Teamcenter product correspond with the Teamcenter Release cycle\.
2. Features that have a completed TRA may be launched within a PI, independent of the Teamcenter Release cycle\.
3. The delivery of hotfixes is driven by business urgency\.

### Procedure for TcX\-CApS Coordination on project Handoff

Tcx Team needs to handoff the project to CApS team for customer deployment\. The procedure includes:

1. A Weekly Dry Run meeting attended by members from Development and CApS team conducted as a status and handoff meeting\.
2. Information related to feature testing, status of the testing, summary of issues found are maintained on Microsoft Teams channel\.
3. Release Manager sends a mail publishing the release based on the Release Criteria report\.

## <a id="_Toc140233951"></a>​​TcX Release Criteria

### Release Definition

1. __Update Releases –__ frequent release that does not impact Functional Support teams \(including Legal, thus no changes to copyrights, Trademarks, Patents, new OEM partnerships, Export compliance issues, or new OSS\)
2. __Technical Release \-__ Impact to Functional Support teams \(Legal, Security, Support\)\. No impact to marketing, price book, patents\.

### Release Criteria

The TeamcenterX Release Criteria are the same as Teamcenter Release Criteria with the following extensions\. __Screenshots or other evidence must be attached to the release object\.__

#### Risks

__Only “accepted” unresolved risks on the associated solution release__

#### AWS Trusted Advisor

AWS Trusted Advisor report executed on the Dry Run/Production account should not report security issues\. Filter for “AWS Trusted Advisor” only \(as other sources are covered by other criteria\)\. 

![](data:image/png;base64,)

#### AWS Security findings

AWS Security Hub reports Security Score using two different standards\. The score must be measured on a newly deployed TeamcenterX production \(or pre\-production\) environment\. The score can be viewed any time via the Splunk Dashboard: [https://splunk\.sws\.siemens\.com/en\-US/app/securityhub/securityhub\_\_securityhub](https://splunk.sws.siemens.com/en-US/app/securityhub/securityhub__securityhub)  

The individual scores can be viewed at the following

1. [AWS Foundational Security Best Practices v1\.0\.0 by AWS](https://us-east-1.console.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/home?region=us-east-1#/standards/aws-foundational-security-best-practices-1.0.0)  80%
2. [CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark v1\.2\.0 by AWS](https://us-east-1.console.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/home?region=us-east-1#/standards/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark-1.2.0) 80%

#### AWS Inspector Findings

AWS Inspector reports known security vulnerabilities and weaknesses\. The findings must be evaluated on a newly deployed TeamcenterX production \(or pre\-production\) environment\. The findings can be viewed at any time via the Splunk Dashboard, selecting the relevant Project Group and Project Name then “non\-compliant”:

1. [SecurityHub \- Inspector V2 | Splunk 9\.1\.1 \(siemens\.com\)](https://splunk.sws.siemens.com/en-GB/app/securityhub/securityhub__inspector__v2?form.finding_token=*&form.account_token=*&form.saas_token=*&form.region_token=*&form.compliance_token=*&form.scan_token=AWS_EC2_INSTANCE&form.vuln_token=No&form.severity_token=CRITICAL&form.severity_token=HIGH&form.name_token=*&form.id_token=*&form.raw_token=No&form.dedup_token=No&form.create_time_token=No&form.time_token.earliest=-1d%40d&form.time_token.latest=%40d&form.ldap_token=*&form.group_token=*) 
	1. EC2: 0 findings with severity Low or higher
	2. ECR: 0 findings with severity Low or higher 
	3. Lambda: 0 findings with severity Low or higher

#### Aqua findings

*TBD; applicable at future release after procedure and scope defined*

Aquasec is used for identification of security vulnerabilities within container images are run time\.

XCR cluster name and Kubernetes namespace details are required to identify security vulnerabilities applicable to TcX release deployed in clean room environment\.

You can get these details from person who deployed the environment in clean room account

Also extract list of container images running in particular release from \\helm\_charts\\imageversions\.yaml

e\.g\. [helm\_charts/imageversions\.yaml · main · tcx\-containers\-deploy\-automation / tcx\-tenant\-repos\-dev / newtcx06\-prd · GitLab](https://gitlab.industrysoftware.automation.siemens.com/tcx-containers-deploy-automation/tcx-tenant-repos-dev/newtcx06-prd/-/blob/main/helm_charts/imageversions.yaml?ref_type=heads)

- Login to Aquasec
- Go to Security Reports \-\-> Vulnerabilities

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Select TCX from scope drop down \(first box\), Images in second drop down\.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Click on filter \(funnel icon\) on right side \(highlighted in red circle\) and expand environment details 

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Choose applicable Cluster and Namespace from environment details drop down and click on Filter\. 

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Final screen should look like this

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Click on export button right side of the filtered result and choose Compressed CSV

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- It will pop following screen, give description and select export columns as “Aqua Recommended Columns” and click Export\. This will create export job\.
- Again, click on export job and select “Exporter Jobs” this time and click download\. It will download compressed csv file containing image vulnerabilities\.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Extract all SI for Teamcenter, Teamcenter X and Teamcenter Enterprise products from Polarian and type = security issue\.
- Compare CVE id from aqua findings against polarian SI cve record
- If found in aqua and missing in Polarian – raise new SI
- If found in aqua and Polarian
- If SI status is closed, then open new SI
- If SI status is in draft AND applicable to image in question, then ignore \(No new SI\)

Release criteria for container vulnerabilities

- Critical vulnerabilities \- We may not deliver with critical findings
- High Vulnerabilities \- We should not deliver with high findings; if we do, we must have a resolution plan in place, as the high's will have to be fixed within 60 days

#### X\-Ray\-discovered vulns found in Artifactory

*TBD; applicable at future release after procedure and scope defined*

#### Security of dependencies \(e\.g\. Pillar 0\)

TcX heavily depends on Pillar 0; therefore, unmitigated risks in Pillar 0 are inherited by TcX\. TcX requires dependent Pillar 0 components to demonstrate compatible and meaningful release criteria\. Evidence of such must be attached to the release object\.

Criteria must include,

- Static analysis results for IaC
- AWS Inspector results for EC2 and Lambda upon which TcX or dependent components \(K8S\) are hosted
- AWS Security Hub results for EC2 upon which TcX or dependent components \(K8s\) are hosted
- Aqua results on Pillar 0 managed containers used by TcX
- Aqua results on K8S

### Release Criteria \- TeamcenterX on Azure 

The TeamcenterX Release Criteria are the same as Teamcenter Release Criteria with the following extensions\. Screenshots or other evidence must be attached to the release object\.

#### Risks

__Only “accepted” unresolved risks on the associated solution release__

#### Azure Security Posture

__Secure score __from Azure's Microsoft's Defender for cloud determines the overall security posture of subscription\. Security score must be evaluated on a newly deployed TeamcenterX production \(or pre\-production\) environment\. 

The score can be viewed any time via the following dashboard:

 [https://portal\.azure\.com/\#view/Microsoft\_Azure\_Security/SecureScoreDashboard](https://portal.azure.com/#view/Microsoft_Azure_Security/SecureScoreDashboard) \- 80%

![](data:image/png;base64,)

#### Azure Compliance Posture:

Azure __Regulatory Compliance__ in Microsoft Defender for Cloud evaluates and reports adherence to industry standards and regulatory requirements\. There should be no critical findings from below listed regulatory standards:

- Microsoft cloud security benchmark
- ISO 27001:2013
- SOC 2
- CIS Azure Foundations v2\.0\.0

Regulatory Compliance status can be viewed through following dashboard: 

[https://portal\.azure\.com/?feature\.msaljs=true\#view/Microsoft\_Azure\_Security/ComplianceBlade](https://portal.azure.com/?feature.msaljs=true#view/Microsoft_Azure_Security/ComplianceBlade)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

#### Azure Vulnerability Posture

Azure update manager governs security and vulnerability updates of Azure VM's and update status of machines can be viewed through dashboard: [https://portal\.azure\.com/?feature\.msaljs=true\#view/Microsoft\_Azure\_Automation/UpdateCenterMenuBlade/~/overview](https://portal.azure.com/?feature.msaljs=true#view/Microsoft_Azure_Automation/UpdateCenterMenuBlade/~/overview)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The findings must be evaluated on a newly deployed TeamcenterX production \(or pre\-production\) environment\. 

Vulnerability findings are accessible anytime on the Splunk Dashboard by selecting the relevant Project Group and Project Name, then filtering Compliance to "non\-compliant"\.

[Microsoft Defender for Cloud Vulnerabilities | Splunk 9\.3\.2](https://splunk.sws.siemens.com/en-GB/app/cso_azure_dashboards/ms_d4c_vulns?form.finding_name_token=*&form.types_token=*&form.severity_token=*&form.instance_token=*&form.subscription_token=*&form.saas_token=*&form.resource_type_token=virtualmachines&form.compliance_token=*&form.vuln_token=No&form.resource_id_token=*&form.finding_id_token=*&form.raw_token=No&form.dedup_token=No&form.ldap_token=LCS_Zeus&form.group_token=TCX)

- Azure Virtual Machines: 0 findings with severity Critical or High

Note: The Splunk dashboard is currently non\-functional and will be fixed\.

### Procedure for acceptance of release readiness by CApS

The CApS Release Management team performs a dry run\. The criteria for release readiness may include the following\. The CApS team’s processes define the actual criteria\.

1. Successful completion of the dry run\.
2. Any issues discovered are resolved and a clean dry run performed\.
3. Any workarounds required are identified and documented in the Dry Run status spreadsheet\.
